actual_author_read_scope: Complete main text and tables through Discussion, including actual reread of methods, Results and source inconsistencies; bibliography retained. No raw PDF or visual figures.

claims.paraphrase: Native PaW1/pWW0 purification differs from temperature-induced E. coli K-12 single-gene constructs. XylJ alone retained hydratase activity; isolated XylI activity was unstable.

Methods reverse H/I gene functions relative to the final interpretation; one Results sentence reverses 27/28 kDa assignments. Use XylH tautomerase, XylI decarboxylase and XylJ hydratase with these conflicts retained.
The 28 kDa native/3.5 kDa apparent subunit estimates are historical; the authors acknowledged abnormal SDS mobility. They do not establish an eight-subunit enzyme.

Tautomerization and side-activity assays depended on buffer and salts. Six-minute spontaneous conversion was condition-specific; NMR product assignment was personal communication, not a reported experiment.
Decarboxylase and hydratase copurified in a preparation near 130 kDa with two polypeptides. Exact subunit copy numbers were not measured.
Hydratase favored the freshly prepared enol pool. Aged substrate accumulated resistant keto material and an unidentified degradation product; neither historic names nor absorbance assigns exact E/Z.

Decarboxylase used the keto diacid and produced mainly a dienol by spectral estimation. Magnesium dependence and kinetic values belong to those preparations; manganese also accelerated spontaneous conversion.
The hydratase product keto/enol form remained explicitly unresolved. The text/figure product-number inconsistency must not silently decide formal chemistry.

limits: Detailed quantitative assertions remain in the hash-bound predecessor claim ledger, reclassified for the oxidative route.
No direct channeling proof, exact substrate E/Z, universal XylJ partner requirement or seventh acylating step follows.
